report.source_text: For accurate identification, we extracted genomic DNA of the strains and performed polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays targeting the internal transcribed spacer region (ITS) using primers and amplification conditions described previously [2]. PCR products were sequenced and compared in CBS (www.cbs.knaw.nl) and GenBank database (https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/). The ITS sequence of isolates shared 99% identity with the reference sequence for T. interdigitale (CBS 428.63T).

clinician.final_diagnosis: dermatophytosis and keratomycosis caused by T. interdigitale with loss of vision in the left eye
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man presented with chronic multiple ringworm lesions starting near the left eyebrow, progressing over 4 years, and fungal keratitis diagnosed 2 years ago with eventual left eye vision loss. Examination showed extensive erythematous plaques, onychomycosis, conjunctival infection, and corneal ulcer. Fungal microscopy revealed hyaline septate hyphae; cultures from skin, nail, and corneal scrapings grew white downy colonies. Molecular identification via ITS sequencing confirmed T. interdigitale infection. Histopathology of skin biopsies showed parakeratosis, acanthosis, and inflammatory infiltration. The patient received antifungal treatment with clinical improvement and underwent left eye enucleation. There was no recurrence during 3 months follow-up.

Histopathological exam of skin biopsy showed parakeratosis, mild acanthosis, and lymphoplasmacytic infiltration
Ophthalmological examination documented conjunctival infection, corneal ulcer, and vision loss in left eye

Microbiological and molecular studies confirmed T. interdigitale as causative agent in skin and corneal lesions
